extra.message: Affected versions of aiohttp are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. The optimized C HTTP parser in aiohttp validates each fragment of an HTTP request/response line individually against max_line_size instead of the accumulated total. An attacker can split an oversized line across multiple network reads, bypassing the limit and causing excessive memory consumption, leading to denial of service. This affects both server-side request-target parsing and client-side response reason-phrase parsing.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

An attacker can send excessive pipelined requests to an aiohttp server to exhaust memory, leading to denial of service. Only the aiohttp server API is affected; client-only usage is not.

extra.message: Affected versions of aiohttp are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification). aiohttp servers decompress unread compressed request bodies into a single unbounded chunk during lingering-close cleanup, bypassing the client_max_size limit. An attacker can send a small deflate/gzip-compressed request body that decompresses to a very large size, forcing a large transient memory allocation and causing a denial of service.

extra.message: Affected versions of aiohttp are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. aiohttp WebSocket endpoints fail to enforce the max_msg_size memory limit when a peer sends large incomplete WebSocket frame payloads. An attacker (a malicious client against a server endpoint, or a malicious server against a client connection) can send oversized incomplete frames to bypass the size limit and exhaust memory, causing denial of service. Any use of aiohttp server-side WebSocketResponse endpoints or client-side ws_connect connections reaches the vulnerable frame parser.

extra.message: Affected versions of cryptography are vulnerable to Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component / Out-of-bounds Read. The PyPI wheels for the cryptography package statically link a version of OpenSSL that contains security vulnerabilities (including a high-severity use-after-free in PKCS7_verify and several denial-of-service and forgery issues). Any application installed from an affected wheel ships the vulnerable OpenSSL binary, so an attacker may trigger out-of-bounds reads, crashes, or other memory-safety issues through cryptographic operations that reach the bundled OpenSSL code.

cwe: CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
CWE-1395: Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component
metadata.sca-reachable-if: you installed the cryptography package from a PyPI binary wheel not built from a source distribution

extra.message: Affected versions of pyjwt are vulnerable to Improper Authentication / Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature. PyJWT does not reject JSON Web Key (JWK) strings passed as raw HMAC secrets in `HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key`. When a verifier allows both HMAC and asymmetric algorithms and a raw JWK string is supplied as the verification key, an attacker can forge an HS256 token signed with the public JWK string used as the HMAC secret, enabling token forgery and authentication bypass.

cwe: CWE-287: Improper Authentication
CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
